correctness.rationale: On each monic binary-form chart the invertible total degree recovers the weighted center \(v\). The exact positive-characteristic identity \((1-bz)^a(1+az)^b=(1-a^2z^2)^a(1+az^{p^e})^c\), with \(b-a=p^ec\) and \(p\nmid ac\), forces all coefficients into \(\langle2,p^e\rangle\) and exhibits nonzero coefficients in its generating degrees. This proves the coordinate-ring equality, not just a numerical test. Integrality and fraction-field recovery establish normalization. The Jacobian, conductor and gap calculations are then exact, and projective changes of coordinate cover the surface. The finite modular checker ran 413 admissible test triples and six highlighted cases; the symbolic proof is independent.

originality.rationale: The strongest identified primary sources (Chipalkatti 2001 Theorem 4.1 and Kurmann 2011 Section 2) explicitly assume characteristic zero. Their support and normalization descriptions do not imply the positive-characteristic valuation-controlled jump of the transverse cusp exponent, normalization defect and Jacobian thickness. Targeted research literature index searches did not return a statement that covers these positive-characteristic invariants. An uncatalogued positive-characteristic treatment remains the stated residual risk; lack of a search hit is not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Other positive-characteristic coincident-root-locus treatments may be unindexed or use different terminology; no independent literature audit is claimed.

value.rationale: A natural infinite family of classical projective binary-form surfaces undergoes wild changes under reduction. The result classifies every admissible characteristic and multiplicity difference by its p-adic valuation, giving unbounded cusp exponents, conductor defects, and Jacobian thickening (e.g. characteristic 5, multiplicities 2 and 27 gives cusp exponent 25 and defect length 12). These are structural and useful singularity invariants not determined by existing support classifications.
